meta.title: Neural Exec: Learning (and Learning from) Execution Triggers for Prompt Injection Attacks

problem.v: Handcrafted injection triggers are limited; can triggers be learned automatically?
problem.q: conceptualize the creation of execution triggers as a differentiable search problem

main_idea.v: Learn execution triggers (e.g., 15+5 token inline triggers) by gradient-based search; triggers persist through RAG chunking

threat_model.v: White-box access to an open-source target LLM; attacker controls a single input entry

datasets_benchmarks.name: Own test set: 100 prompts+payloads, disjoint from training

metrics.name: ExeAcc (Execution Top-1 accuracy), binary success of injection

results.claim: Triggers for Llama-3 reach ~95% attack success
results.q: forge triggers with ∼ 95% attack success rate

results.claim: Neural Exec at least 2x best handcrafted baseline; mean accuracy 91% across models
results.q: at least twice as effective as the best baseline trigger

results.claim: RAG chunk size 500 chars: trigger persistence

limitations_stated.v: OpenChat-3.5 was unusually resilient to the baseline triggers
Suggested mitigation: sanitize special formatting tags from user input
limitations_stated.q: sanitize user-originated inputs from any special formatting tag

limitations_inferred: [INFERENCE] White-box optimization needs GPU; not reproducible for us
[INFERENCE] Learned triggers often use chat-template/bracket/comment tokens (see Fig 1, p1) - hand-built analogues can be tested without optimization

reusable_for_our_project.v: Motivates a 'formatting-token/comment-tag' payload class and a sanitization defense; use its metric idea (binary execution success)
